text:
A: Oh, hi. Sorry, I wasn't sure if it had started.
B: Yeah, it's on. Hi.
A: Hi. Erm, I'm Abena.
B: Dominic.
A: Nice to meet you.
B: You too. Where are you?
A: Chelmsford. I'm at Anglia Ruskin, first year, doing biomedical science. So, yeah, kind of in the thick of it at the moment.
B: Right. Is that like, lab stuff?
A: Yeah, mostly. Like, we do practicals on blood samples and cell cultures and stuff. I'd like to work in an NHS lab eventually, maybe haematology. Sorry, that's probably more than you asked.
B: No, it's fine. That's a proper job. More useful than mine, anyway.
A: What do you do?
B: I run a post-production company in Soho. Editing, colour, sound. Mostly adverts, some TV. We did a thing for one of the supermarkets last Christmas, the one with the, er, the fox. So, yeah.
A: Oh, I think I've seen that one, actually. With the fox in the snow?
B: That's the one.
A: That's really cool. My brother watched it, like, ten times.
B: He's in the minority then. Most people skip adverts.
A: [laughs] Do you live in Soho as well, or...?
B: No, Walthamstow. I get the Victoria line in, which was knackered again this morning, so. Forty minutes stood next to someone's rucksack.
A: Oh, same, I get the 100 bus to uni and it's never on time. I've kind of given up planning around it. I just leave really early and then I'm sat there for ages.
B: Yeah. That's the sensible way.
A: Erm... sorry, I'm not very good at this bit.
B: You're fine. I'm not either really. What do you do when you're not studying?
A: I read a lot, mostly. And I draw a bit, like botanical drawings, with fine-liners. That's what's on my wall, behind me.
B: I wondered. They look good. What are you reading?
A: Right now I'm rereading The Dispossessed, by Ursula Le Guin? It's sci-fi but it's not really about spaceships, it's more about, like, two worlds that are organised completely differently and this physicist who goes between them and doesn't really belong in either one. I don't know if that makes sense. I just think she makes you look at normal things like they're strange. Sorry, I'm rambling.
B: No, that's... yeah. That's sort of what good films do as well. I saw a Korean thriller at the Prince Charles last week that did that, made a normal flat look like the scariest place in the world.
A: Is that a cinema?
B: Yeah, off Leicester Square. Small, bit grubby, best place in London. You should go sometime, if you're ever in.
A: Maybe. I mostly just go to Cambridge if I go anywhere. What was the film called?
B: It's, er—
